## Problem 0

I use one R Markdown file for this homework. The local data files are in the
`data` folder, and I use relative paths to read them. I load the NOAA
data from the `p8105.datasets` package. The R Markdown file uses
`github_document` output.

## Problem 1

### Data description and missing values

```{r noaa-data}
data("ny_noaa")
```

The dataset has `r format(nrow(ny_noaa), big.mark = ",")` observations and
`r ncol(ny_noaa)` variables. Each row is one daily record from a weather
station. There are `r n_distinct(ny_noaa$id)` stations in New York State, and
the dates range from `r min(ny_noaa$date)` to `r max(ny_noaa$date)`.

The variables are station ID (`id`), date (`date`), precipitation (`prcp`),
snowfall (`snow`), snow depth (`snwd`), maximum temperature (`tmax`), and
minimum temperature (`tmin`). The original precipitation unit is tenths of
a millimeter. The original temperature unit is tenths of a degree Celsius.
Snowfall and snow depth are already in millimeters, according to the
[course data description](https://p8105.com/dataset_noaa.html).

```{r noaa-missing}
missing_summary <- ny_noaa %>%
  summarise(across(everything(), ~ sum(is.na(.x)))) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    everything(),
    names_to = "variable",
    values_to = "missing"
  ) %>%
  mutate(percent = 100 * missing / nrow(ny_noaa))

knitr::kable(
  missing_summary,
  digits = 3,
  col.names = c("Variable", "Missing observations", "Missing (%)")
)
```

Missing data are a major issue. Maximum and minimum temperatures are missing
for about
`r sprintf("%.3f", missing_summary$percent[missing_summary$variable == "tmax"])`%
and
`r sprintf("%.3f", missing_summary$percent[missing_summary$variable == "tmin"])`%
of the records. Some stations report only a subset of the weather variables.
Missing values may affect comparisons across stations and years.

### Data cleaning and common snowfall values

```{r noaa-clean}
noaa_df <- ny_noaa %>%
  mutate(
    year = lubridate::year(date),
    month = lubridate::month(date),
    day = lubridate::day(date),
    tmax = as.numeric(tmax) / 10,
    tmin = as.numeric(tmin) / 10,
    prcp = prcp / 10
  )
```

I keep the original date and add separate year, month, and day variables.
I convert maximum and minimum temperatures to numeric values in degrees
Celsius, and precipitation to millimeters. Snowfall and snow depth remain in
millimeters. The cleaned dataset has `r ncol(noaa_df)` variables.

```{r snow-counts}
snow_counts <- noaa_df %>%
  filter(!is.na(snow)) %>%
  count(snow, sort = TRUE) %>%
  slice_head(n = 6)

knitr::kable(
  snow_counts,
  col.names = c("Snowfall (mm)", "Number of observations")
)
```

The most common snowfall value is 0 mm, with
`r format(snow_counts$n[snow_counts$snow == 0], big.mark = ",")` observations.
This is reasonable because many days have no snowfall. Other common values
include 25, 13, 51, and 76 mm. These values are close to whole-inch or
half-inch amounts, so rounding or conversion from inches may explain the
pattern.

### Average maximum temperature in January and July

```{r station-summary}
station_month_df <- noaa_df %>%
  filter(month %in% c(1, 7)) %>%
  group_by(id, year, month) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_tmax = mean(tmax, na.rm = TRUE),
    observed_days = sum(!is.na(tmax)),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  filter(is.finite(mean_tmax)) %>%
  mutate(
    month = factor(month, levels = c(1, 7), labels = c("January", "July"))
  )

cold_july <- station_month_df %>%
  filter(month == "July") %>%
  slice_min(mean_tmax, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE)
```

```{r station-temperatures, fig.width=12, fig.height=5}
ggplot(station_month_df, aes(x = year, y = mean_tmax, group = id)) +
  geom_line(color = "#2C7A7B", alpha = 0.2, linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_point(color = "#2C7A7B", alpha = 0.3, size = 0.5) +
  facet_wrap(~ month, nrow = 1) +
  labs(
    title = "Station temperatures in January and July",
    x = "Year",
    y = "Average maximum temperature (°C)",
    caption = "Each line is one station. Monthly means use available days."
  )
```

July is much warmer than January. January temperatures also show larger
changes across years. Many stations have colder January temperatures in
1982, 1994, and 2004. Stations often move in the same direction within a
year, which suggests a shared regional weather pattern.

There are some unusual station averages. For example, station
`r cold_july$id` has a July average maximum temperature of
`r sprintf("%.3f", cold_july$mean_tmax)` °C in `r cold_july$year`, based on
`r cold_july$observed_days` observed days. This value is much lower than most
other July averages. It could reflect local conditions or a data problem,
so I would check the station record before treating it as an error. Some
station-month averages use very few observed days, so they may be less
reliable.

### Daily temperatures and snowfall distributions

```{r temperature-snow, fig.width=12, fig.height=5.5}
temperature_plot <- noaa_df %>%
  filter(!is.na(tmin), !is.na(tmax)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = tmin, y = tmax)) +
  geom_bin_2d(bins = 70) +
  geom_abline(
    slope = 1,
    intercept = 0,
    linetype = "dashed",
    color = "#D55E00"
  ) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(transform = "log10") +
  labs(
    title = "Daily temperatures",
    x = "Minimum temperature (°C)",
    y = "Maximum temperature (°C)",
    fill = "Observations"
  ) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")

snow_plot <- noaa_df %>%
  filter(snow > 0, snow < 100) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = factor(year), y = snow)) +
  geom_violin(fill = "#A4C4BC", color = NA, scale = "width") +
  geom_boxplot(width = 0.15, outlier.shape = NA, fill = "white", linewidth = 0.3) +
  scale_x_discrete(
    breaks = as.character(c(1981, 1986, 1991, 1996, 2001, 2006, 2010))
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Positive snowfall below 100 mm",
    x = "Year",
    y = "Snowfall (mm)"
  )

temperature_plot + snow_plot + plot_layout(ncol = 2)
```

Maximum and minimum temperatures have a strong positive relationship.
The two-dimensional bins show the full dataset of observed temperature
pairs without too many overlapping points. The dashed line marks equal
maximum and minimum temperatures. Most observations are above this line,
as expected. However, there are
`r sum(noaa_df$tmin > noaa_df$tmax, na.rm = TRUE)` records with minimum
temperature greater than maximum temperature. These records need further
checking.

For snowfall greater than 0 and less than 100 mm, the distributions are
broadly similar across years. The median is about 25 mm, and larger amounts
are less common. There is no clear steady increase or decrease in this
restricted range. The plot describes snowfall on the selected station-days;
it does not show total annual snowfall or events of 100 mm or more.
